::: {.callout-note}
Federal agencies have spent decades governing the identities of their workforce. The citizen-facing surface — the 300 million Americans who interact with federal agencies as beneficiaries, taxpayers, petitioners, and applicants — has received far less governance attention. Book_22 makes that surface visible: who the external identity subjects are, how assurance levels govern what agencies can ask them to prove, how Login.gov provides shared proofing infrastructure, and how the cross-agency attribute exchange — agencies serving as both vendors and customers of each other's authoritative identity data — is surfaced and governed in UIAO.
:::
